Subject: NimbleCare renewal: uplift framework, invoice tie-out & legal timing

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the time last week. NimbleCare’s renewal window is coming up and you mentioned a mid-contract capacity increase for Q3 (additional Dedicated capacity for peak batch jobs). I pulled together two uplift frameworks so we can align commercial + billing flow before legal reviews. I attached a short PDF that lays out:

- Option A: Staged uplift (3-month ramp, invoice pro-rata for month of change, staged discount of 7% -> 4% -> 2%)
- Option B: Immediate top-up with co-term to annual renewal (one invoice, blended effective rate, 10% discount on uplift units)

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Procurement prefers a single consolidated invoice (Option B) or monthly pro-rata adjustments (Option A).
- Confirm if NimbleCare needs the uplift billed to the existing PO or a new PO reference.
- Any SLA carveouts needed for the higher reserved capacity? We can offer a 99.9% latency target for the Dedicated pool under Option B but need procurement sign-off.

I put Karthik on copy for pricing mechanics and Marissa for legal timing. If it helps I can run a short one-pager for finance that maps invoice rows to the PO fields your AP team expects.

Next step: quick 30-minute call to pick A vs B and agree timeline for legal redline. Are you available Wed 6/23 10:00–10:30 PT?

Thanks,
Sofia

Sofia —

Appreciate the clear options. Quick answers up front: procurement prefers a single consolidated invoice if we can keep the payment on the existing PO (PO-2247). That tends to simplify our AP. Finance will need a line item breakdown showing the prior committed units vs uplift units and effective month-by-month rates for accounting.

On SLA, we need a short note in the amendment that the Dedicated pool throughput is guaranteed for the uplifted units (we can live with 99.9% latency as you propose) and an explanation of how Redwood will cascade to fallback nodes in case of regional capacity pressure. Legal will want the fallback behavior explicit.

I’m free Wed 6/23 10:00 PT. Let Procurement know and I’ll forward to them to lock the PO referencing.

Cheers,
Alex

Thanks Alex / Sofia —

I pulled the workbook referenced in the attachment and validated the monthly proration math. A couple of items to flag from pricing ops perspective:

1) If NimbleCare selects Option A (staged uplift), we recommend a temporary uplift SKU with a 90-day staged discount ladder as Sofia proposed. That keeps the existing contract intact and avoids mid-period co-term accounting.
2) Option B (single invoice + co-term) is cleaner for AP but will require annualizing the uplift for your FY reporting — I estimate NimbleCare would see a slightly lower effective per-unit price in year 1 but will need an amendment to move billing lines to the renewal date.
3) If you want the uplift to be subject to the same usage overage thresholds, we should explicitly call that out in the amendment; otherwise the uplift will be reserved units that don't count toward the base usage true-up.

I updated the spreadsheet (nimblecare_uplift_estimate.xlsx) to include: invoice row examples for PO-2247, journal-friendly description text (for finance), and a suggested credit memo flow if we need to reverse a staged invoice.

Sofia: for the 6/23 call I can take the pricing walkthrough and have one slide that maps the invoice rows to NimbleCare PO fields. Marissa: want to flag any legal caveats we should be ready to accept/avoid.

—Karthik

Thanks all — quick legal note ahead of the call:

- We can accommodate a single consolidated invoice (Option B) using an amendment that attaches the uplift SKU lines to the renewal. Legal will want a short exhibit that: (a) calls out the PO number, (b) states the effective date of the uplift, and (c) defines fallback behavior if we need to route requests to a compatible model variant or alternate region.
- On SLA language: we cannot commit to region-level capacity guarantees outside of the Dedicated pool commitment. We can, however, include a latency SLO for uplifted units with a defined credit formula (credits per minute of outage tied to monthly uplift spend). That gives you predictability without overcommitting on regional capacity.
- Timeline: if Procurement can sign an LOI on 6/25 we can issue an amendment draft same day; legal redlines typically take 3–5 business days depending on change requests.

I’ll be on the 6/23 call to capture redline asks.

Best,
